title: Most People
gist_ar: نقاش: 'معظم الناس' جملة ممكن تكون صح ومفيدة بصفر، لأنها بتخبّي إن الدعم هشّ.

before_listening.en: A panel discussion about one phrase. Listen for the pollster's MAIN criticism of it.
before_listening.ar: نقاش عن جملة واحدة. ركّز على النقد الأساسي من خبيرة قياس الرأي.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: Every guest on this programme this month has told me what most people want. Dalia, you actually measure it.

segments.speaker: Dalia
segments.text: And that is why I almost never use the phrase. 'Most people' is doing something dishonest in nearly every sentence it appears in. Take last week's figure: sixty-one per cent support the scheme. That is most people, in a sense. But of those sixty-one, fewer than half could describe what the scheme does, and a third said they would oppose it if it raised their own costs, which it will. So 'most people support it' is both true and useless.

segments.speaker: Minister
segments.text: With respect, all of politics works like that. Neither of us has a better instrument. Every mandate in every parliament rests on a number that thin.

segments.speaker: Dalia
segments.text: I agree, and that is not a defence. It is the problem. The honest sentence is longer: a majority express support, few understand the detail, and support falls sharply when costs are mentioned. Nobody puts that on a poster.

segments.speaker: Minister
segments.text: Because a poster with that on it loses.

segments.speaker: Host
segments.text: So is there any question where the answer is stable?

segments.speaker: Dalia
segments.text: Yes. Almost all of them, if you ask twice, six months apart, and count only the people who say the same thing both times. That group is usually about a quarter. Every serious campaign is fought over the other three quarters, and each of them will tell you that they are most people.

gist_question.q: What is the pollster's main criticism of the phrase?
options: The underlying polling data itself is simply inaccurate and cannot be trusted at all
It can be technically true while hiding that few understand and support is fragile
Politicians should stop commissioning polls altogether

questions.q: What is true of the sixty-one per cent who support the scheme?
questions.q_ar: إيه الصحيح عن الـ 61% اللي مؤيدين المشروع؟
options: Fewer than half could describe what it does
All of them understand what it will cost
They would all still support it if their costs rose

questions.q: How does the minister respond to the criticism?
options: He disputes the underlying figures and the way they were gathered
He says all politics rests on numbers that thin
He agrees the scheme should be abandoned

questions.q: Which group does she say gives the same answer twice?
questions.q_ar: أنهي مجموعة قالت إنها بتدّي نفس الإجابة مرتين؟
options: About a quarter of those asked
About three quarters of those asked
